generation.explanation: With 100% annual interest compounded n times a year, each period earns 1/n interest, so your $1 becomes (1 + 1/n)ⁿ after one year. Annual compounding gives $2, twice-yearly gives $2.25, and monthly gives about $2.61. As compounding becomes more frequent, the balance approaches e ≈ $2.71828—not infinity. Drag the yellow point to explore how the balance approaches this limit.
